reading.body:
Arizona's data center map counts 56 facilities, but only 4 publish power specifications, and this Tempe entry is not a confirmed operating data center at all.

The entry rests on an OpenStreetMap node at coordinates that reverse geocode to a building at 2005 West 14th Street, Tempe, with no business name attached. No operator website, business registration, or press coverage naming J-Curve Technologies at that address could be confirmed, and research status is recorded as exhausted. The name itself is more common in finance and economics than in the technology industry. Nothing in the record shows server rooms, colocation space, or data center equipment.

For AI scaling, the number that matters is power, and the only published Arizona figure here is 512 MW across 4 facilities. A count of 56 mapped sites cannot be converted into a capacity estimate, because 52 of them publish nothing. This entry contributes no megawatts and cannot be ranked against the 4 that do, so it should not enter any calculation of grid load or siting constraint in the state.

What the data does not say is that the building is not a data center. It says no public evidence confirms one, which is a weaker claim. The record also cannot speak to statewide capacity, since the unpublished majority is unmeasured rather than zero. The site sits about 2.5 miles from Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport and more than 20 miles from other rows in its batch, so no shared building or campus links it to them.
